examples.name: Basic action menu
examples.description: A plain list of action rows with leading icons, no search or selection.
examples.jsx:
<Menu
  aria-label="Matter actions"
  showSearch={false}
  sections={[
    {
      id: 'actions',
      items: [
        { id: 'rename', label: 'Rename', leadingElement: <EditIcon spacing="spacious" decorative />, onSelect: handleRename },
        { id: 'duplicate', label: 'Duplicate', leadingElement: <CopyIcon spacing="spacious" decorative />, onSelect: handleDuplicate },
        { id: 'delete', label: 'Delete', leadingElement: <DeleteIcon spacing="spacious" decorative />, onSelect: handleDelete },
      ],
    },
  ]}
/>

examples.name: Searchable menu with a heading
examples.description: The default searchable shape, filtering a named section by typed text.

examples.name: Checkbox-style multi-select section
examples.description: Each row independently opts into selectionType='checkbox'; the leading glyph is Figma's own CheckboxFillIcon/CheckboxEmptyIcon, colored selected/subtle to match - not a real Checkbox control.

examples.name: Radio-style single-select section
examples.description: Each row opts into selectionType='radio'; only the consumer's own state ensures a single selected row. The leading glyph is Figma's own RadioCheckedIcon/RadioUncheckedIcon.

examples.name: Keeping a containing Dropdown Menu open after a choice
examples.description: Menu never closes anything itself; a containing Dropdown Menu closes after an item's onSelect unless it calls event.preventDefault() - here, so a checkbox row can be toggled repeatedly.
examples.jsx:
<Menu
  aria-label="View options"
  showSearch={false}
  sections={[{
    id: 'view',
    items: [{
      id: 'drafts',
      label: 'Show drafts',
      selectionType: 'checkbox',
      selected: showDrafts,
      onSelect: (event) => {
        event.preventDefault();
        toggleDrafts();
      },
    }],
  }]}
/>

examples.name: Loading state
examples.description: Replaces the sections area with a Spinner and a custom label while data loads.
examples.jsx: <Menu aria-label="Matter actions" loading loadingLabel="Loading matters…" showSearch={false} sections={[]} />

antiExamples.name: Nesting a real Checkbox inside leadingElement
antiExamples.jsx:
<Menu
  aria-label="View options"
  sections={[{
    id: 'view',
    items: [{
      id: 'showDrafts',
      label: 'Show drafts',
      selectionType: 'checkbox',
      selected: checked,
      leadingElement: <Checkbox checked={checked} onChange={handleToggle} />,
    }],
  }]}
/>
antiExamples.reason: Each row renders as a real <button>. Nesting Checkbox's real <input> inside it is invalid HTML (a focusable control inside another one) and creates two conflicting ways to activate the same row - one via the button's own onClick, one via the checkbox's onChange. Use a decorative icon/glyph instead and let selected/selectionType carry the real state, or toggle the row's own onSelect.

antiExamples.name: Nesting a Menu inside a Dropdown Menu
antiExamples.jsx:
<DropdownMenu open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
  <Button>Actions</Button>
  <Menu sections={[{ id: 'a', items: [{ id: 'delete', label: 'Delete', onSelect: handleDelete }] }]} />
</DropdownMenu>
antiExamples.reason: DropdownMenu has no children-as-content slot: its one child is the trigger, and it builds its own Menu from the sections you pass it (and closes after a choice). Pass sections to DropdownMenu directly instead of nesting a Menu.
